service_text: Removed fan shroud and disconnected fan motor. Removed fan motor and took fan bracket apart. Installed new fan bracket and Re-installed fan motor. Tightened everything down and ran fan in test mode to check for noises. Motor ran smooth and found no more vibration noises from fan bracket. Put fan shroud back on and turned unit back on.
service call replace faulty motor seized

10/5/19 gain access to roof where unit is located. Found vfd tripping on over current fault. Test motor windings to ground also to check resistance between windings. Tested ok. Reset vfd and attempt to run motor. Motor shaking badly on startup and eventually tripped on over current. Remove belts and reset vfd. Motor still shaking and still tripping on over current. Call Alan Henderson with carrier tech support to confirm that motor is bad and to approve replacement. Alan advised me to inspect internal rotor of motor for rust. Confirmed that there is rust on motor rotor. Alan recommended replacing motor and will only approve this once. Will order motor.    10/5/19 troubleshoot unit.    11/8/19  Schedule with customer for motor replacement. Remove old motor from unit, install new motor, remove pulley from old motor and install on new motor. Wire in new motor. Will return to install belts, align and perform startup on motor.    11/11/19  Return to site and check in with customer. Get access to roof. Install new belts supplied by customer. Align pulleys and correctly tension belts. Grease fan bearings and clean up site. All OK

Responded to call for supply fan making whining noise. Arrived at site. Checked in with security. Met with customer. Obtained access to rooftop and shown to problem unit. Found fan making noise. Used navigator to put unit in test mode. Ramped supply fan speed up to 95%. Checked fan motor amps. 9.5, 9.3, 8.9 amps. Fan noise increased with speed. LOTO power to unit. Removed unit side panel for better access to fan section. Checked belt tension and pulley alignment. Proper tension and alignment. Removed drive belt. Checked fan shaft bearings. No play and seem to be in good working condition. Checked for play in drive shaft. No play. Spun motor by hand to find bearings making noise. Restored power to unit and ran ran motor with no belt. Bearings whining at higher speeds. Motor will need to be replaced. LOTO power to unit and reassembled. Replaced side panel. Restored power to unit and put back in normal operation. Explained findings to customer. Roped tools and equipment down from rooftop. Checked out with customer.  Drove to Sigler and picked up new motor and belt.  Picked up unistrut gantry from shop. Arrived on site and checked in with security. Gained access to rooftop and rigged motor up to rooftop. Did a walkthrough around unit and walkthrough on how motor was going to be rigged. Assisted nick in removing old motor that was seized out of place and its components and cleaned off hub. Applied to new motor and rigged new motor in place and reconnect electrical. Aligned motor pulley and fan pulley and assure shaft had no play secured new motor and applied new belt. Power equipment and check operation of motor and watch for any play or unusual sound. All ran efficiently with no problems with proper cooling temp. Rigged old motor down and set in nicks van to be dropped off to shop with rigging equipment. Checked out with customer. Drove to chickasha, at job site checked circuit B operation. Found circuit still shutting off on high head pressure, with cps magnet manually opened liquid line solenoid valve. Cycled circuit B on with the same results. Verified voltage to solenoid. Found condenser exv causing the restrictions via temperature of piping. Ran condenser exv to 100% on navigator, cycled circuit B on with no results. Will come back tomorrow to recover refrigerant, pull out exv and check mechanical operation after verifying voltage outputs from exv module.  Drove to chickasha, at job site contacted tech support.   Case #00920120   On the phone, checked configuration settings and found everything fine. Checked voltages to condenser exv, looking for 6vdc but did not have voltage. Switched condenser exv plug to the bypass exv plug to drive open condenser exv. Drove condenser exv open and cycled B circuit on. Ohmed out windings on exv, had 79ohms from green to red and 79 ohms from white to black. Found a bad exv board.   In order to finish start up switched exv boards from other 40 ton. Will order and switch exv boards after completion of start up paperwork.    Picked up exv board, drove to chickasha. At job site removed old board and installed new board. With the new board installed checked exv outputs by putting unit into test. Received 5vdc when tested. Cycled unit into cooling mode and checked operation. Circuit B no longer trips. Cleaned up job site and drove to okc.
Not working  bad exv board  Replaced

Friday.. configured unit for outdoor air humidity sensor per instructions that was sent with sensor. Ran B compressors in service test. Found bad board that controls EXV. Ordered new board. Friday.. scheduled time to shut down unit. Replaced board. Tested EXV in service test. Ran compressor in service test.

Arrived onsite to insulate blower and exv board section to attempt to eliminate condensation that is causing exv board failures. Replaced bad exv board and downloaded the proper software, exv is now operating properly. No need to replace condensing exv. System operating properly.

Picked up material to repair the condensate drain line. Cut out the broken fitting in the condensate drain pan and fabricated a new condensate drain line with trap. Turned the unit back on and checked the operation. The supply air temperature was at 68 degrees, looked over the set points and lowered the occupied cooling setpoint from 75 to 72 and lowered the supply air setpoint from 68 to 55 degrees

Upon arrival both carry rooftop units were shut down due to burning order according to facility maintenance. Check supply fan motor and power exhaust motors and found no problems. Checked VFD and bypass controller and found no problems. Check via the parameters and protective limits and found no problems. Found no alarm history and VFD buffer.     Ramped up all motors in both units to 100% and ran for several hours and monitor. Found no problems with any motors on either of the two units.     Doors on filter section appear to have blown open and damaged condensate traps, they will need to be repaired.
Disconnect handle jammed up and set screw not holding the shaft. Labor to install new parts correctly.

Continued work on leak repair     Brought all equipment to rooftop. Put nitrogen in system to pin point leak. Repaired leak on discharge line of compressor on circuit A. Changed liquid line filter drier. Put 240 psi nitrogen into system to check for leaks, no leaks detected. Put system into vacuum. Once system is low enough, charged 30.5 lbs of R410A into circuit A. Started unit in test mode and had a discharge pressure of 340 and 115 suction pressure. Unit is discharging 55 degree air. Returned unit to normal operation and enabled circuit A compressors. Cleaned up work area and disposed of garbage off site.     Arrived on site and gained access to rooftop. Discharge pipe on Circuit A has broken off and charge has been lost. Removed piece of pipe that was left in compressor. Replaced liquid line filter drier. Repaired line for discharge. Pressurized with 40 psi nitrogen to test over night. Checked with soap bubbles and initial check at 40 psi is pass. Turned unit back on and disabled Circuit A to allow Circuit B to run. Cleaned up work area and will return in the morning.  Arrived on site and gained access to rooftop. Brought equipment to work area and set up for work. Circuit A held nitrogen pressure over night. Blew off and began pulling vacuum. Broke vacuum with nitrogen 3 times to bring microns down as far as possible. Began charging with 22.5 lbs of r410a. Compressor 1 running good but when compressor 2 started there was a sound of mechanical failure. Turned off power and tested compressor 2 for any shorts or grounds. All check to be good. Compressor is going into alarm for Reverse Rotation. Tried changing leads and ran compressor. Same alarm returned and there was no change in pressures. Compressor has failed mechanically. Retrieved unit and compressor information and sent for replacement. Locked out circuit a and returned unit to normal operation with circuit b running. Cleaned up work area and disposed of garbage off site.

Service tech found that the contractor had failed due to the springs dropping out of the contactor causing the   compressor to single phase. The contacts looked OK, however the springs looked to be overheated   because of the color of the springs. I agreed to cover up to $450.00 toward the repairs.

Met with Tim Burke on site. Inspected machine. Picked up supplies from United. Pulled charge from unit. Began disassembling compressor electrical and found shorted wire in compressor pecker head. Tested compressor electrically and found no issues. Replaced contactor. Recharged machine and ran in test mode. Unit still tripping off. Swapped ground fault protection boards between A2 and B1. Retested. Unit operating properly. No need to replace compressor.
